title: How hard is it to vibe code a roblox game
author: Aggravating-Aerie175
selftext: I'm not an experienced game dev whatsoever and I don't even particularly like Roblox.  How hard would it be though to create a slightly profitable roblox game with pretty much just vibecoding?  Roblox games are essentially the slop of games so I imagine it wouldn't be as hard as making an actual good indie game?

comments.author: Outside_Specific_820
comments.body:
not hard at all. People cannot see your scripts. If you built, make the UI, hire someone to make an original icon and thumbnail then no one will know your game was vibe coded imao

go ahead and vibe code it, you can do it, 100%.

But yeah its a lot easier to make roblox games then true indie games.

comments.author: _TheLastGamer
comments.body: If you are asking this question, then it will be really hard.

comments.author: derAres
comments.body:
It’s funny that profitable and slop are the only words you used to describe Roblox 🤔…  
To answer your question: making a somewhat similar game is doable with AI. Profitable and scalable are two entirely different questions.

replies.author: Aggravating-Aerie175
replies.body: I’m hypothetically talking more about profitable.  Also what was funny about profitable and slop being the only two words I used to describe Roblox.  Is that not an apt description of most of the popular Roblox games?

replies.author: derAres
replies.body: What about calling it highly successful minigame ecosystem? Because that is what it is. Roblox is a legendary success and you‘re dismissing and disrespecting that, while still wanting to milk the formula somehow.

replies.author: Aggravating-Aerie175
replies.body: I’m not saying Roblox the company isn’t a massive success.  I’m saying that a majority of its games are slop.  Yes there are some great ones but let’s not act like most of the things on there are pure works of art

replies.author: derAres
replies.body: They are not, but that is okay, as those will not rise to the top. You really have to look at it like an ecosystem. No one stops you from throwing slop on there, bit if people do not find enjoyment in it the slop will be nearly invisible as it falls to the bottom of the lists. And everything you do see at the top I would never call slop, even if it lools like a trashy 2002 browser game, because were people not playing it, it would’nt be up there.

replies.author: silasfelinus
replies.body: I suspect you are seeing what look like low-effort visuals, but disregarding whatever went into making a satisfying gameplay loop.

comments.author: silly_bet_3454
comments.body: it shouldn't be too hard to make the most basic of basic games. However, a lot of a game is really more about assets, like the visuals in the game, rather than just code, and coding agents are much less useful in that area. Also, there is a vast vast vast difference between making a "game" and a "profitable game" unless your definition is charging under a dollar and selling your game to 10 people. Actually making a game that will draw people's interest is like 99% about having good ideas and play testing your game and thinking about fun and the user experience and only 1% about the "coding"

comments.author: BenTheSodaman
comments.body:
Hi Aerie,

Initial thoughts are: 

Relatively not difficult to vibe code the game. 

To monetize it to where it pays for itself and more (whether you're assigning yourself minimum wage per hour invested or picking a market rate as a benchmark plus the cost of your assets/tools/subscriptions to develop it), that's uncommon in the Roblox ecosystem. 

With vibe coding expanding that ecosystem even more. 

Fable 5 can handle the creation, but you'd need to get it done before July 7 and under 50% of the weekly usage limit. Afterwards (unless things change), you'd be paying for Fable 5 at the API rates and that could easily put most in the red and keep them there. The feedback you get from players (if any at all) will take you beyond July 7.

And it helps a helluva lot more if it's a game that you yourself could yourself sinking playtime into with friends as your ideas better align with your playerbase. Versus making a product for a userbase you can't relate to. 

e.g., I can't relate to the 6 7 game. It's not something I have or would play in the foreseeable future. And I can make a Roblox game with that as its core principle. I'm delusionally confident that I can monetize the product to pay for itself and then some plus keep players coming back. 

I'm also confident that the nearly all the games I'd like to develop and play, if adapted to Roblox, would absolutely not pay for themselves. And for a chunk of them, even if they were free, would have very few players without an influencer spotlight on it. But I'd play the shit out of them.
